stories.title: Fuel excise duty cuts to be phased out from November
stories.summary: The Cabinet has agreed that cuts to excise duty on petrol and diesel will be phased out over a period from November to the end of February. Last week, the Government announced that it was pausing the increases in excise planned for September and October amid rising fuel prices. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris got Cabinet approval for this measure this morning. Mr Harris believes the move will provide certainty to households at a time of volatility on global energy markets.

stories.title: Vhi to increase prices by average of 2.75% from October
stories.summary: Vhi is to increase the prices of its health insurance policies by an average of 2.75% from the beginning of October. This will be the provider's second price rise this year, after it announced a 3% average hike across its plans that took effect in March. Vhi is the largest health insurance company in Ireland, with around 1.2 million customers - roughly half of the entire market. The latest increases will see the price of its EnhancedCare 250 plan, which is especially popular among young adults, go up by €22 a year to €1,300 for an adult.

stories.title: Mater to compensate employee for racial discrimination
stories.summary: One of the country's largest hospitals has been ordered to pay €10,000 compensation for racially discriminating against a Nigerian-born employee when suspending him primarily based on the colour of his skin. At the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) adjudicator, Penelope McGrath BL ordered Mater Misericordiae University Hospital to pay €10,000 compensation to healthcare assistant, Paul Agbons for discriminating against him on the grounds of race when suspending him for six days from 6-12 June last year. In making the award, Ms McGrath stated that the employer had to balance two very difficult situations and that she was mindful of the fact that the suspension only lasted six days. On 13 June 2025, the hospital told Mr Agbons "that he did not have a case to answer" arising from the patient's complaint.

stories.title: Call for independent CUH staff review amid safety fears
stories.summary: A group of consultants at Cork University Hospital (CUH) has called on Minister for Health, Jennifer Carroll MacNeill, to appoint an independent assessor to examine staffing issues at the hospital. Last week, Jennifer Kearney, Chief Executive of CUH wrote to the HSE, raising serious safety concerns about the hospital. In her letter, Ms Kearney said she did not believe it was safe to enter the winter period with the level of staffing uncertainty that she said currently exists. Yesterday, Minister Carroll MacNeill dismissed those concerns, stressing that CUH, like every other hospital, has to manage within its budget.

stories.title: Ireland has highest EU rate of paid film and TV streaming
stories.summary: Ireland has the highest proportion of internet users paying for film, television series or sports streaming services in the European Union, according to new figures from Eurostat. Seperate commercial research has found a similer rate of uptake, while also indicating that Irish consumers may be spending almost €2 billion a year on streaming services. Eurostat says that almost two thirds of Irish internet users, 63.9%, had a paid subscription to at least one of these services in 2025. The figure was higher than in any other EU member state, with Denmark next at 61.1% and the Netherlands at 59.2%.

stories.title: Poison helpline reports 4% rise in calls in 2025
stories.summary: The National Poisons Information Centre (NPIC) reported 11,455 enquiries last year, a 4% rise in calls from medical and healthcare staff and the public, its latest figures show. Around 60% of calls concerned children under the age of 15, and most of the poisonings occurred within the home. Of the overall medication enquiries, paracetamol is the commonest drug involved, followed by ibuprofen. The 24-hour centre is based at Beaumont Hospital in Dublin and advises nationally on how to deal with suspected poisonings.

stories.title: Floods on Nepal-Tibet border described as 'apocalyptic'
stories.summary: Kerry based explorer and mountaineer Pat Falvey has described the devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border as "apocalyptic". Mr Falvey who has been to Nepal over 70 times and considers it his "spiritual home" said the area where it happened was "very populated" and without a warning system unlike other parts of Nepal. Almost 1,400 people, including around 800 foreigners, are missing across Nepal and Tibet, authorities said, after a wall of mud and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river, sending catastrophic flash floods ⁠through towns and valleys. Mr Falvey who leads expeditions to Nepal said he "really got a fright" and thought it was "AI" when he saw the initial videos.

stories.title: Andy Burnham begins first official Northern Ireland visit
stories.summary: British prime minister Andy Burnham is making his first official visit to Northern Ireland today. He will speak to a group of young people about a range of issues including the cost of living before meeting the main political parties. Demands for more money are likely to dominate his discussions with the politicians as the Stormont Executive has still not agreed its annual budget. Sinn Féin, the DUP and other parties have all blamed Westminster, accusing it of short-changing Northern Ireland when it comes to per capita spending.

stories.title: HSE-run nursing home inspection found infection outbreak
stories.summary: An inspection by the Health Information and Quality Authority (HIQA) of a HSE-run nursing home based in Munster discovered the early start of an outbreak of infection which resulted in transmission from two residents to 11 residents and five staff. Inspectors who visited the centre in March were informed that two residents had been unwell and had symptoms of an infection 24-48 hours previously, but they were better. Following a review of the nursing notes, an immediate action was given to the staff nurse to inform public health that a possible outbreak of infection was in progress. According to the report the HSE did not follow infection prevention contol guidance.

stories.title: Unite warns of a 'winter of strikes' in the public sector
stories.summary: The Unite trade union has said that its members in the public sector have voted overwhelmingly in favour of industrial action if the Government fails to make a meaningful offer on pay. Yesterday, the Prison Officers Association said its members have also backed industrial action over the same issue. Similar ballots have also been announced by other public sector unions including Fórsa, SIPTU and the INMO. The previous public sector pay deal expired on 30 June, and formal talks have yet to begin on a successor agreement.

stories.title: Highest number of taxi drivers recorded in 10 years
stories.summary: The taxi sector is attracting more new drivers with the highest number on record in 10 years. A total of 1,893 licences were issued last year, bringing the total number to 27,891. The National Transport Authority (NTA) said the figures, along with its latest research, shows that there is a "strong interest" in joining the sector. "We see that business is there and people want to chase that business," said Director of Transport Regulation Kevin O'Brien.

stories.title: New levy for sustainable flood insurance fund proposed
stories.summary: Insurance Ireland is proposing a new levy of €24 per insured household to be placed into a "sustainable flood insurance fund" to address what it calls "Ireland's flood insurance protection gap". The levy is among a number of measures put forward in a report by the group representing insurers, which it said would allow homeowners to continue to access sustainable flood cover amid increased flooding risk due to climate change. It said the fund should be designed to ensure households in higher-risk areas can access flood insurance, where cover would otherwise be unavailable. Insurance Ireland said the Government could consider rebalancing existing insurance levies alongside the proposed new one that could allow its proposals to be introduced "with broadly no net additional cost to the average household".

stories.title: Over 4,000 complaints made to European Consumer Centre
stories.summary: The European Consumer Centre Ireland (ECCI) handled 4,182 complaints last year, and recovered €421,000 for Irish and other consumers from businesses across European Union. According to the 2025 ECCI annual report, Irish consumers accounted for almost half (48%) of all complaints and enquiries it dealt with. The centre assists consumers based in Ireland who have a problem with an EU business in any member state. Air travel accounted for the largest share of complaints last year (34%), while just over half of all complaints were referred by partner consumer centres across Europe.

stories.title: Talks due at WRC aimed at resolving Oberstown dispute
stories.summary: Talks will be held at the Workplace Relations Commission today in a bid to a resolve a dispute over staffing levels at the Oberstown Children Detention Centre in Dublin. Members of the Fórsa trade union employed at the campus have staged a series of work stoppages and are threatening to hold a 48-hour strike next week. Fórsa said the industrial action is being taken to highlight the issue of safe staffing levels at Oberstown. The union said it will attend the talks at the WRC, but plans for next week's 48-hour strike remain in place.

stories.title: Irish woman and her husband found dead at Spanish resort
stories.summary: Police in Spain are investigating the deaths of an Irish woman and her husband at a coastal resort south of Valencia. Homicide squad officers are leading the investigation, although police say the possibility they suffered an accident while they were in a jacuzzi has not yet been ruled out. Their bodies of the woman, aged 45, and the man, aged 50, were discovered yesterday afternoon in a residential estate called Cap Blanc in Cullera, a town of around 25,000 people south of Valencia. Local police were mobilised along with the Civil Guard, the force which is leading the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: Man, woman injured after car crashes through M50 barrier
stories.summary: A man and a woman in their 80s have been seriously injured after the car they were travelling in crashed through a barrier before coming down a verge onto the M50. The incident happened at the flyover by Junction 10 Ballymount beside the slip road onto the southbound lane of the motorway. Emergency services attended the scene around 3.20pm, and the two occupants of the car were brought to hospital with serious injuries. The road was closed while the scene was preserved for a forensic examination, but it has since reopened.

stories.summary: New data released by the HSE shows wide variations in performance in delivering cancer treatment for patients. The information on the National Cancer Control Programme covers 2025 and the first half of this year, and details Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy (SACT), radiation oncology, and time to surgery for certain tumours, when surgery is the first treatment. The data was obtained from the HSE by Sinn Féin health spokesperson David Cullinane from a Parliamentary Question. "If you take radiotherapy, the figures are going in the wrong direction," he said. "21% of patients were not seen within the recommended 15 working days.

stories.title: Parton visit to Kerry GAA legend's pub was 'monumental'
stories.summary: Dozens of tourists and locals have been visiting Páidí Ó Sé's Pub in Ceann Trá near Daingean Uí Chúis, Co Kerry, where they gathered to pay respects to Dolly Parton. The country music star, who died yesterday at the age of 80, famously visited the pub, owned by Kerry football legend Páidí Ó Sé, in 1990. She sang Coat of Many Colors there, accompanied by musicians Steve Cooney and Seamus Begley, before taking home Páidí Ó Sé's own 1985 All-Ireland Kerry jersey - which she later said was still framed in her home. She signed off her performance at the time with "thank you very much and welcome to Dinglewood".

stories.title: 38 children killed on roads in five-year period - RSA
stories.summary: A total of 38 children under the age of 16 have been killed on Irish roads in the last five years, according to new data from the Road Safety Authority. The authorIty said that 620 children suffered serious injuries in the same time period from 2021 to 2025, which represents just under 10% of all those badly hurt in road crashes. Of the 658 children either killed or seriously injured, almost half were pedestrians while over a quarter were passengers in a vehicle. More than 30 children were e-scooter users, while a dozen children were drivers.

stories.title: Ferry passengers to require passport for UK travel
stories.summary: Passengers travelling between Ireland and the UK with Irish Ferries and Stena Line will be required to carry their passports from next month. Irish Ferries said the rule change will apply to passengers on their Dublin to Holyhead and Rosslare to Pembroke routes from 28 September. While Stena Line said its passengers will have to show their passports on their Dublin to Holyhead and Rosslare to Fishguard crossings. Currently, passengers are not always asked to show a passport but have sometimes been required to have another form of photo ID such as driving licences and national identity cards.

stories.title: Man detoxing from vaping HHC thought he was 'dying'
stories.summary: A 22-year-old man who was hospitalised in recent days after years of smoking vapes containing HHC has said he thought he was dying when he started to experience withdrawal symptoms. HHC is a semi-synthetic cannabinoid which is stronger than cannabis and has been illegal in Ireland since last year. "I thought I was dying, to be honest I didn't think I was going to make it through," he said. "I didn't think those vapes could have caused something like that. "I was afraid for my life, I really was, I didn't know what was going on with me."Jakub said he was introduced to HHC vapes four years ago by his friend.

stories.title: Railway watchdog issues safety notice after 'near miss'
stories.summary: A railway safety watchdog has issued a safety notice to Iarnród Éireann about the importance of planning work before accessing the railway, following a "near miss" last month when two rail workers managed to move to safety from a fast approaching train with just seconds to spare. The Railway Accident Investigation Unit (RAIU) said a safe system of work (SSOW) must be planned with red zone working only used as a last resort when all other safer options have been considered and ruled out. Red zone working means the railway line remains completely open to trains travelling at normal operating speeds without any restrictions. The safety notice arose following an incident on 13 July on the line between Ballyhaunis, Co Mayo and Castlerea, Co Roscommon when the Westport-Dublin Heuston passenger service approached two railway staff working under red zone conditions at a speed of 108km/h.

stories.title: School historical sexual abuse commission to begin work
stories.summary: The Commission of Investigation into the Handling of Historical Child Sexual Abuse in Schools has written to survivors to say it is preparing to commence its work. The correspondence says a national survey will be carried out this Autumn seeking information from survivors, relatives representing people who cannot participate, and others who witnessed or have relevant information about abuse. The Commission of Investigation was established after a Scoping Inquiry into Historical Sexual Abuse in Day and Boarding Schools Run by Religious Orders, published its findings in 2024. It revealed there were 2,395 allegations involving 884 alleged abusers across 308 schools between 1927 and 2013.
